title: Beyond Supra-Competitive Outcomes: Collusive Behaviour in Deep Reinforcement Learning for Optimal Execution Games
abstract: arXiv:2610.00619v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In this paper, we extend earlier findings of supra-competitive outcomes in optimal-execution games by identifying a learned punitive mechanism that deters deviations and provides behavioural evidence of collusion. We investigate this mechanism in a two-player, finite-horizon Almgren-Chriss liquidation game. Independent proximal policy optimisation agents with access to within-episode price and action histories achieve costs below the Nash benchmark. We identify a profitable deviation by training against the mean learned liquidation schedule, then impose its first trade on one of the original agents. The opponent responds by accelerating liquidation. This response more than offsets the deviator's gain in every run and both player roles, while leaving the punisher's average payoff materially unchanged relative to not punishing under the same deviation. translated_title: 超越超竞争结果：深度强化学习在最优执行博弈中的串谋行为
translated_abstract: 在本文中，我们通过识别一种学习到的惩罚机制，扩展了关于最优执行博弈中超竞争结果的早期研究，该机制能够阻止偏离行为并提供串谋存在的行为学证据。我们在一个双人、有限期限的Almgren-Chriss清算博弈中研究这一机制。拥有回合内价格与行动历史信息的独立近端策略优化（PPO）智能体实现了低于纳什基准的成本。我们通过针对学习到的平均清算计划进行训练来识别出一个有利可图的偏离策略，随后将该偏离策略的首笔交易强加给原始智能体之一。对手随即通过加速清算作出回应。在每一次运行以及双方玩家角色中，这种回应都完全抵消并超过了偏离者的收益，同时相对于在同一偏离情形下不进行惩罚的情况，惩罚者的平均收益基本保持不变。惩罚者在保持自身平均收益的同时，给偏离者施加了更大的损失……
tldr: 本文发现深度强化学习智能体在最优执行清算博弈中会自发学习出一种惩罚机制——通过加速清算来惩罚偏离者并使其收益受损，为算法之间形成隐性串谋提供了行为学证据。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies a learned punitive mechanism in deep RL optimal execution games, where agents punish deviators by accelerating liquidation, providing behavioral evidence of emergent collusion between algorithms.
